sources: MONDAY Oct 5 2026 RUN (06:20 UTC, pre-US-open - market fields are Friday Oct 2 closes plus live Monday Asian/European session where available). HEADLINE: OIL FINALLY BROKE LOWER - BRENT 101.49, DOWN ON THE WEEK - AND THE MOVE INDEX 'RECORD' TURNS OUT TO BE A STALE QUOTE. OIL - THE G7 RELEASE IS WORKING: Brent 101.49 USD/Bbl (TradingEconomics, Oct 5 live), DOWN 0.75-0.94 pct on the day and now DOWN roughly 0.8 pct on the week, versus 102.25 at the Friday Oct 2 settle. This is the first genuine downside in crude since the shock began and the trend is downgraded from flat to DOWN. Two drivers, both supply: the G7's agreed release of up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel from emergency reserves, and Middle Eastern crude exports running above pre-war levels on four of the seven days in the final week of September (HDFC Sky, Oct 5). WTI near 90, down about 1.2 pct. NOTE A GENUINE SPLIT IN THE TAPE: Gulf News (Oct 5) reports Brent at 102.31 and UP 0.07 pct, with Murban at 110 and the Brent-WTI spread above 11 dollars on Strait of Hormuz security premia, tanker shortage, insurance costs and surged VLCC freight. Two of three sources cluster at 101.3-101.5, so 101.49 is carried, but the seaborne risk premium has NOT disappeared - it has been pushed into the Brent-WTI and Murban differentials rather than the flat price. BOND VOL - RETRACT THE RECORD, IT IS A STALE QUOTE: MOVE carried at 105.74 (Friday Oct 2 close). CRITICAL DATA FLAG: both Investing.com and TradingView TVC-MOVE this run served 107.29/107.30 at minus 0.78 pct, and Investing.com explicitly dates that quote FEBRUARY 10. The two venues are serving the SAME stale tick, so the apparent fresh print above the 106.61 Oct 1 record is NOT a real observation and must not be read as a new high. MacroMicro 403, Baltic/paid sources unreachable. Independently confirmed anchors: 101.82 on Sep 29, the first close above 100 since the spring, after a 35 pct monthly surge seen only eight times since 2008 (Benzinga). Level roughly plus 14 pct over one week. Trend up, level carried, source still unwired - this is now the second-worst data gap on the dashboard after BDTI. CREDIT - THE PAYROLL-REACTION PRINT HAS NOT LANDED YET: HY OAS 324bp (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2, 3.24 pct dated Oct 1), UNCHANGED from yesterday's run because the Oct 2 observation had not been released at run time (01:20 CDT; FRED posts mid-morning ET). Confirmed independently by MacroRadar at 3.24 pct, 74th percentile of the last decade, versus a 10-year average of 3.21 pct and up 17.4 pct over twelve months. The sequence remains nine consecutive widening sessions: 268 (Sep 18), 266 (Sep 21), 268 (Sep 22), 273 (Sep 23), 280 (Sep 24), 293 (Sep 25), 302 (Sep 28), 308 (Sep 29), 312 (Sep 30), 324 (Oct 1) - 56bp with no retracement. The Oct 1 print still PREDATES the payroll report entirely. Today's release is the single most important number on the dashboard: it is the first credit observation that contains the plus 29k payroll reaction. Trend up. RATES - THE STEEPENING IS ENTIRELY LONG-END, AND THAT IS THE POINT: 2s10s 0.45 (FRED T10Y2Y, Oct 2), versus 0.46 (Oct 1), 0.41 (Sep 30), 0.37 (Sep 29), 0.32 (Sep 28). The weekly decomposition now resolves cleanly: 10y 5.28 pct, UP 11bp on the week; 2y 4.83 pct, up just 2bp; 30y 5.63 pct, up 14bp. The curve steepened because the long end sold off, not because the front end rallied - and it did that in a week that delivered a plus 29k payroll print and priced out a hike. Long rates refusing to fall on bad growth news is the stagflation tell, and it is now confirmed in the term-structure decomposition rather than inferred. FED: October hike odds below 23 pct from 64 pct one week earlier. BREAKEVENS STILL ANCHORED: 5y5y forward 2.35 pct (FRED T5YIFR, Oct 2), 2.36 on Oct 1, 2.35 on Sep 28. Brent has round-tripped 30 dollars down, 6 up and back through flat, the labour market cracked, the long end sold off 11bp, and long-run inflation expectations have moved 1bp. Four tests in both directions; still has not broken. Flat. EQUITY VOL - DIVERGENCE WITH CREDIT INTACT: VIX 15.31 (Cboe, Oct 2 close), down 6.59 pct on the day as equities rallied on the weak payroll print, but UP about 3 pct versus 14.87 on Sep 25, so the weekly trend is up. FRED VIXCLS has not yet posted Oct 2 and still shows 16.39 for Oct 1. S&P 500 7,722.72 (minus 0.27 pct on the week), Nasdaq 27,190.86 (plus 0.45 pct), Dow 51,176.96 (minus 1.26 pct), Russell 2000 2,832.90. Third consecutive run with equity vol and credit spreads pointing opposite ways. FINANCIAL CONDITIONS - THE RELEASE THAT MATTERS IS WEDNESDAY: NFCI minus 0.548 for the week ending Sep 25 (FRED NFCI), no new print at run time, NEXT RELEASE OCT 7. Sequence minus 0.559 (Aug 28), minus 0.560 (Sep 4), minus 0.558 (Sep 11), minus 0.553 (Sep 18), minus 0.548 (Sep 25) - half a basis point of tightening across five weeks against 56bp of HY widening, a MOVE above 100 and an 11bp long-end selloff. Loosest of the cycle. Carried flat. Seven weeks of divergence and Wednesday is the first chance to resolve it. DOLLAR: DXY 101.95 (Investing.com real-time, Oct 5; Friday Oct 2 close 101.93, plus 0.95 pct on the week, third consecutive weekly gain). Roughly unchanged on the session. DATA NOTE: TradingEconomics shows 102.34 and plus 0.41 pct for Oct 5, which is an outlier - Investing.com (101.95), Dealplexus (101.92) and the CNBC weekly wrap (101.93) all cluster near 101.9, so the TE CFD proxy is discounted. Trend up; 52-week high is 102.21 and the index is pressing it. COPPER/GOLD 1.57, unchanged for a third run. Copper 6.51 USD/Lbs (plus 0.35 pct on the day but about minus 3 pct on the week on weakening Chinese industrial activity); gold 4,152.08 USD/t.oz (plus 0.29 pct on the day, minus 5.74 pct on the month). 6.51/4152.08*1000 = 1.57. Both legs still falling together on the week, so the ratio remains uninformative - it is not signalling a growth impulse. Flat. Global liquidity 1 (stable). REAL ECONOMY - NO NEW PRINTS, TWO LANDING THIS WEEK: ISM manufacturing 54.5 for September (ISM, Oct 1), down from 54.6, prices paid 77.9 - expansionary but decelerating with cost pressure building. Trend down. Initial claims 197k for the week ending Sep 26 (FRED ICSA; 198k, 198k, 207k, 207k before it), NEXT RELEASE OCT 8 - still the one indicator that has not confirmed the payroll weakness, and the key number this Thursday. Flat. SAHM RULE 0.00 for September (FRED SAHMREALTIME, released Oct 2), up from minus 0.07 in August, minus 0.03 in July, plus 0.07 in June - the first non-negative print of this cycle. Trigger is plus 0.50, so this is direction, not a recession signal. Next print Nov 6. Trend up. UMich consumer sentiment 48.1 (final September, a four-month low, one-year inflation expectations 4.6 pct), next print Oct 9. Building permits 1,403k (August; 1,433k July, 1,374k June, 1,410k May), next release Oct 20. LEI y/y about minus 0.7 pct (August index 99.5, six-month growth minus 0.1 pct), next release mid-October. CARRIED STANDING ASSUMPTIONS, no free live source found this run: SOFR-OIS 0bp, EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis minus 10bp (only CME/ECB methodology pages reachable, no live quote). BDTI DATA FLAG - FOURTEENTH consecutive run carried at 4,899 and formally non-informative. StockQ now renders an Oct 2 row with a BLANK value; Investing.com frozen at 1,107 dated 31/03; MacroMicro, Barchart inaccessible; Baltic Exchange subscription-only. Public commentary puts the real BDTI all-time high near 1,900, so 4,899 is not on a comparable scale and must NOT be read as a level. Wire a paid source or drop the tile. PICTURE: the oil leg of the stagflation squeeze is being dismantled by policy and by supply - Brent is down on the week for the first time, and the G7 release plus recovering Gulf exports did it. That removes one blade of the scissors. What it does not remove is the other: the long end sold off 11bp in a week that produced a plus 29k payroll print, credit has widened nine straight sessions without retracement, and the broadest measure of financial conditions has registered half a basis point of it across five weeks. Two of today's three headline numbers are carries rather than prints - HY OAS and MOVE both await releases or working sources - so today's run is better read as a positioning run than a signal run. The two real changes are oil turning down and the term-structure decomposition confirming that the steepening is a long-end selloff rather than a front-end rally. WATCH: today's HY OAS print, the first credit observation that contains the payroll reaction, and whether it makes ten sessions; the NFCI release on Oct 7 after seven weeks of divergence; initial claims on Oct 8, which have contradicted the payroll weakness at 197k for three weeks; UMich on Oct 9; whether the 10y holds 5.28 or breaks; whether DXY takes out the 102.21 52-week high; whether Brent keeps falling through 100 or the Hormuz premium rebuilds via the Brent-WTI spread; and wiring a working MOVE and BDTI source, which are now the two blind tiles.
